title: All-Purpose Chicken Seasoning
subtitle: a golden, savoury rub for roast, baked or grilled chicken any night
imageAlt: A small glass jar of golden-orange chicken seasoning with a spoonful on a cream plate beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: about ½ cup: 4 batches of 2 tbsp

breakdown: Garlic and onion powder, 1 tbsp each
Brown sugar, dried thyme, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Use a clean, completely dry jar and spoon: any moisture makes the blend clump.
Check the dates on your jars; spices older than a year lose most of their flavour.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Measure everything into a small bowl.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk with a fork until the colour is even, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Jar it
steps.text: Spoon into a clean, dry jar, seal and label it with the name and date.

steps.title: Use it
steps.text: Use 2 tbsp per 1 kg chicken pieces (or a whole chicken) with 1 tbsp oil. Roast until 74°C (165°F) in the thickest piece, or 82°C (180°F) in the thigh of a whole bird.

fixIt.fix: Moisture got in; break it up with a fork and keep the jar away from the stove's steam.
The spices are old; replace the oldest jar and remix.
Make the next batch with half the salt and salt the food separately.

saleTip: No Frills bulk bins sell spices by weight: buy just a few tablespoons for a fraction of the jar price.
swap: Leave out any one spice you don't have; the blend still works.
leftovers: Keeps for months; a small jar makes a nice gift.
doneness: No cooking. Season raw meat or fish with a clean spoon (never dip a spoon that touched raw meat back into the jar) and cook the food to its safe temperature.
source: Based on common Canadian grocery-store and test-kitchen versions of this blend (Club House, Canadian Living, Serious Eats), made mild for us.
prepAhead: Make a double batch; it keeps 6 months in a sealed jar.
reheat: Nothing to reheat. Leftovers cooked with it reheat to 74°C (165°F).

fancy.note: Lemon pepper twist: dried lemon zest and extra pepper.

items.name: lemon
items.note: zest only, dried 1 hour on a plate

addSteps.title: Dry the zest
addSteps.text: Spread the lemon zest on a plate and leave it 1 hour (or microwave 1 minute in 20-second bursts) until dry, then stir it in.

plating: Pour into a small glass jar.
Hand-write the label with the date.
Tie twine around the lid if it's a gift.

why.0-4: A little brown sugar helps the skin brown and balances the salt.
why.0-0: Paprika gives that golden-red colour without any heat.

funFact: Chicken is Canada's most-eaten meat, at roughly 35 kg per person a year.

keeps.room: 6 months in a sealed jar, away from heat and light
keeps.note: no need; the cupboard is best (the freezer adds moisture)

pairs: rubbed under and over the skin
